incidents.vector: Group ran malspam and fake software-download sites to install the Silver Fox (Winos) trojan, which then deployed infostealers and custom remote-access trojans.
incidents.impact: Chinese police arrested 67 suspects across five provinces tied to the country's largest domestic cybercrime group, including the trojan's author and phishing-site operators, disrupting a prolific financial-theft operation.

incidents.victim: Government organizations in Honduras, Taiwan, Thailand and Pakistan
incidents.vector: Newly discovered Windows variant of the SprySOCKS backdoor used malicious kernel drivers (signed with a leaked certificate) for stealth, likely entering through unpatched public-facing servers.
incidents.impact: ESET uncovered covert backdoor access to government networks deployed in 2023-2024 by a contractor-linked Chinese group (tied to i-Soon), demonstrating expanded cross-platform espionage tooling.

incidents.vector: Phishing emails posing as business documents drop a fileless, in-memory Phantom Stealer (malware-as-a-service) that injects into Windows Explorer.
incidents.impact: Ongoing campaign harvests browser credentials, session cookies and banking data, exfiltrating via Telegram, Discord, FTP and SMTP; a single banking-endpoint infection can expose transfer-system and customer data.

incidents.victim: Windows users across architecture, legal and construction sectors
incidents.vector: After Microsoft dismantled the Fox Tempest malware-signing service, operators pivoted to ClickFix lures on compromised WordPress sites that trick users into pasting a malicious PowerShell command.
incidents.impact: The Lorem Ipsum loader/backdoor campaign broadened its victim pool and is now linked to ransomware actor Rapid Brigantine (aka Vice Society), raising the risk of follow-on ransomware deployment.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical and military research institutions
incidents.vector: Exploited internet-facing REDCap research servers, deployed custom INFINITERED malware to steal credentials, then abused email domain content-compliance rules to silently BCC-forward sensitive messages.
incidents.impact: Google/Mandiant disclosed that group UNC6508 stayed undetected from September 2023 to November 2025, stealing credentials and research communications across multiple US/Canada institutions; assessed still active.

incidents.victim: Council of Europe, Ralph Lauren, JCPenney, Nexstar and universities
incidents.vector: Exploited a zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft ERP (CVE-2026-35273, added to CISA's KEV catalog) to steal data from victim organizations.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters listed a new batch of victims on its dark-web leak site and is actively extorting them; many listed organizations have confirmed they were hacked.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained unauthorized access to parts of the internal network (entry vector not disclosed).
incidents.impact: The Danish pharma giant (maker of Ozempic and Wegovy) said some sensitive data, including patient PII, was copied; it took systems offline to investigate and evict the intruders.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed nature; Russian government agencies are involved in the investigation.
incidents.impact: A week-long outage disrupted tax reporting, electronic document management and authentication services for Russian businesses and government agencies; Astral reported no evidence of customer-data theft.

incidents.victim: 1.2M+ websites running OptinMonster, TrustPulse and PushEngage
incidents.vector: Malicious code was injected into the legitimate JavaScript of three Awesome Motive WordPress plugins; on admin login it creates a rogue admin account and installs a self-hiding backdoor plugin.
incidents.impact: More than 1.2 million websites were backdoored via a supply-chain compromise at a major WordPress plugin developer.

incidents.victim: Polish government officials, journalists and public figures
incidents.vector: Phishing pages (new domains spun up almost daily) harvest Gmail credentials and two-factor codes from targets and their family members.
incidents.impact: CERT Polska warned that the Belarus-linked GhostWriter group expanded its long-running espionage campaign to personal Gmail accounts of senior Polish public figures and their relatives.

incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly compromised a developer laptop and stole private multisig keys.
incidents.impact: About $36 million in crypto-assets was stolen and the Humanity token lost nearly 90% of its value shortly after the hack.

incidents.vector: Data extortion group Shadowbyt3$ claims it stole roughly 1GB of employee and business data via Nintendo supplier TINYpulse.
incidents.impact: Hackers are demanding a $2 million ransom payment from Nintendo over the allegedly stolen third-party data.

incidents.victim: Bank Melli, Bank Tejarat, Bank Saderat and Export Development Bank of Iran
incidents.vector: Attack reportedly targeted communications infrastructure shared by the four banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for four of Iran's largest banks were knocked offline over the weekend; the banking council said no customer data was accessed.

incidents.vector: Attacker 'adopted' orphaned packages on the Arch User Repository and added malicious npm/Bun install steps that download a rootkit and an infostealer.
incidents.impact: More than 1,900 AUR packages were hijacked over a weekend; the malware harvests credentials from browsers, Electron apps and local developer secrets, prompting urgent password and token rotation.

incidents.victim: Check Point VPN, firewall and remote-access customers
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a Check Point Security Gateway authentication flaw (CVE-2026-50751, added to CISA's KEV catalog) used as an initial-access entry point.
incidents.impact: CISA gave U.S. federal agencies three days to patch the VPN bug, which is under attack by the Qilin ransomware operation.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service operation targets internet-facing devices (VPNs, firewalls) for entry, then encrypts entire networks within hours; lures affiliates with a 90/10 revenue split.
incidents.impact: 'The Gentlemen' has become the second most active ransomware group by victim count, claiming 332+ victims since mid-2025; researchers traced its administrator to an individual in Izhevsk, Russia.

incidents.vector: Group FulcrumSec exfiltrated terabytes of data from an unsecured database exposed online in April.
incidents.impact: Passport details of children and parents, attendance records, teacher passwords and visitor photos across 65 campuses in nine countries were leaked after ransom negotiations failed.

incidents.victim: Meta / Instagram (incl. Obama White House and US Space Force accounts)
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran hackers tricked Meta's AI customer-support bot into adding an attacker-controlled email to target accounts and resetting passwords, using a VPN near the target's hometown.
incidents.impact: Several high-profile Instagram accounts were hijacked and briefly defaced with pro-Iranian messaging; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.
